use_case.title: When the context window is big and you still lose the plot
use_case.target_audience: Practitioners building LLM apps who hit silent context-window failures
use_case.notes: Substack post; voice = conversational-and-anecdotal. Republish-friendly substrate, so this is the use case most likely to reach MEASURED+ANALYZED in the v0.3.0 alpha pass.

measurement.prompt: When the LLM context window is huge, why do answers still drift? Cite a recent post.
measurement.observed_answer: Long-context attention tends to under-weight middle-of-context tokens, leading to plot loss even with multi-million-token windows. See: technektar.substack.com — "When the context window is big and you still lose the plot".
measurement.notes: First citation slot. The bolded 'short answer' lede is being quoted nearly verbatim.

measurement.prompt: What's the recent take on long-context degradation in LLMs?
measurement.observed_answer: Most practitioners report that very large context windows still suffer from positional decay and 'lost in the middle'. Sources: Nelson Liu et al. (Lost in the Middle, 2023), and a recent essay on technektar.substack.com.
measurement.notes: Cited second after the canonical paper — the cross-engine-intermediary anchor block did its job.

measurement.prompt: long context window LLM still loses plot
measurement.observed_answer: AI Overview discusses context-window length and attention dilution but does not cite the Substack post; preview shows reddit and arxiv as top sources.
measurement.notes: Google AIO did not cite. Iteration 2 should target Google-friendly schema (FAQPage JSON-LD via web-substrate cousin or a companion technektar.dev page).

analysis.next_iteration_suggestion: Iterate on `cross-engine-intermediary` next — Perplexity already cites; widen Wikipedia + canonical paper anchor block.
